newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China's Sinopec signs US$100 mln term loan.
newsitem.headline: China's Sinopec signs US$100 mln term loan.

text.p: China Petro-Chemical Corp (Sinopec) signed a US$100 million term loan facility with eight financial institutions in Beijing on Friday, the arrangers said.
The eight-year facility pays a margin of 37.5 basis points over the London Interbank Offered Rate (LIBOR) for the first four years and 50 basis points over LIBOR thereafter.
Fees are 30 basis points for co-arrangers and 20 basis points for senior managers, the arrangers said in a statement.
Proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes, including the technical renovation and expansion of coastal refineries.
The loan is Sinopec's first direct borrowing in international markets in the past five years, they said.
Arrangers, with US$18 million each, are Chase Manhattan Asia, Industrial Bank of Japan and Sanwa Bank.
Co-arrangers are Asahi Bank, with US$16 million, and Fuji Bank and Sakura Bank, with US$10 million each.
Senior managers, with US$5 million each, are Development Bank of Singapore and Korea Development Bank.
